translations.literal: On day xinhai, an edict stated that matters in the earlier constitutional preparation still remained incomplete; each ministry and bureau was instructed, according to the prior format and each office's responsibilities, to report in stages for the Compilation and Review Office to check, after which imperial approval would be followed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day, an edict said constitutional prep was unfinished and told each ministry to report in stages to the Compilation and Review Office for approval.

sentences.zh: 是秋，免雲南會澤被水逋賦，楚雄等縣及湖南漵浦被水額糧。

translations.literal: That autumn, flood arrears in Huize, Yunnan, and quota grain in Chuxiong and other counties and in Xupu, Hunan, were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, flood taxes were forgiven in Huize, Chuxiong, and Xupu.

sentences.zh: 發帑十萬賑湖北、湖南災民。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand taels from the treasury were issued to relieve disaster victims in Hubei and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: 100,000 taels were sent to relieve flood victims in Hubei and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 復賑甘肅災，廣東風災水災，廣西、浙江、黑龍江、福建水災。

translations.literal: Relief was again given for disasters in Gansu; wind and flood disasters in Guangdong; and flood disasters in Guangxi, Zhejiang, Heilongjiang, and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: More relief went to Gansu, Guangdong wind and flood victims, and flooded Guangxi, Zhejiang, Heilongjiang, and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲寅，見日使伊集院彥吉於勤政殿。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiayin: the Japanese envoy Ijuin Hikokichi was received at Qinzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In month 10, jiayin, Ijuin Hikokichi of Japan was received at Qinzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 廣州、肇慶等屬颶風為災，諭施急賑。

translations.literal: Guangzhou, Zhaoqing, and other districts suffered hurricane disaster; urgent relief was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Hurricanes hit Guangzhou and Zhaoqing; the court ordered urgent relief.

sentences.zh: 戊午，賜達賴宴於紫光閣。

translations.literal: On day wuwu, a banquet was given the Dalai Lama at Ziguang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day, the Dalai Lama was feasted at Ziguang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，皇太后聖壽節，停筵宴。

translations.literal: On day renxu, the empress dowager's birthday; banquets were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day, the empress dowager's birthday, court banquets were canceled.

sentences.zh: 達賴祝嘏，進方物，懿旨加封誠順贊化西天大善自在佛，歲賜廩餼萬金，遣歸藏。

translations.literal: The Dalai Lama offered birthday congratulations and presented tribute; by empress-dowager rescript he was further ennobled as the Buddha "Sincere and Obedient, Praising Transformation, Great Benevolent Lord of the Western Heaven," granted ten thousand taels in annual stipend, and sent back to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The Dalai Lama congratulated the empress dowager and brought gifts; she gave him a new Buddhist title, 10,000 taels a year, and sent him back to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上疾甚。

translations.literal: On day renshen, the emperor's illness became grave.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day, the emperor fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 懿旨，醇親王載灃之子溥儀在宮中教養，覆命載灃監國為攝政王。

translations.literal: By empress-dowager rescript, Prince Chun Zaifeng's son Puyi was to be raised in the palace; Zaifeng was again ordered to supervise the realm as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Cixi ordered Puyi, son of Prince Chun Zaifeng, raised in the palace and made Zaifeng regent.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，上疾大漸，崩於瀛台涵元殿，年三十有八。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, the emperor's illness reached its crisis; he died at Hanyuan Hall on Ying Terrace at the age of thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day, the emperor died at Hanyuan Hall on Ying Terrace, aged thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 遺詔攝政王載灃子溥儀入承大統，為嗣皇帝。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict named Regent Zaifeng's son Puyi to enter and succeed to the great succession as heir emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The death edict made Zaifeng's son Puyi heir emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇太后懿旨，命嗣皇帝承繼穆宗為嗣，兼承大行皇帝之祧。

translations.literal: By empress-dowager rescript, the heir emperor was ordered to succeed as heir to Muzong and also to carry the line of the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Cixi ordered the new emperor to succeed Muzong's line and Dezong's line together.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年正月己酉，上尊謚曰同天崇運大中至正經文緯武仁孝睿智端儉寬勤景皇帝，廟號德宗，葬崇陵。

translations.literal: First year of Xuantong, first month, day jiyou: the posthumous title Tongtian Chongyun Dazhong Zhizheng Jingwen Jingwu Renxiao Ruizhi Duanjian Kuanqin Jing Emperor was conferred, the temple name Dezong was fixed, and burial was at Chongling.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong 1, month 1, jiyou: the full posthumous title was granted, the temple name Dezong was fixed, and he was buried at Chongling.

sentences.zh: 論曰：德宗親政之時，春秋方富，抱大有為之志，欲張撻伐，以湔國恥。

translations.literal: Commentary: When Emperor Dezong personally held government, he was still in the prime of life, cherished great ambitions of achievement, and wished to raise the whip of punishment to wash away the nation's humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: When Dezong ruled in person, still young, he aimed to strike hard and wipe away national shame.

sentences.zh: 已而師徒撓敗，割地輸平，遂引新進小臣，銳意更張，為發奮自強之計。

translations.literal: Soon afterward armies and teachers were broken in defeat, territory was ceded and peace bought, and he then brought in newly risen junior ministers, keen to remake policy, as a plan for vigorous self-strengthening.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat and ceded territory, he turned to new ministers for a bold reform program.

sentences.zh: 然功名之士，險躁自矜，忘投鼠之忌，而弗恤其罔濟，言之可為於邑。

translations.literal: Yet men seeking fame were rash and self-conceited, forgot the caution of not striking the rat lest the vessel be broken, and did not care that their plans could not succeed — to speak of it is enough to wring the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ambitious reformers were reckless, ignored the risks, and pressed plans that could not work — a painful story.

sentences.zh: 洎垂廉再出，韜晦瀛台。

translations.literal: When the curtain was drawn again and rule resumed from behind the screen, he withdrew in obscurity to Ying Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager ruled again, he was confined in seclusion on Ying Terrace.

sentences.zh: 外侮之來，釁自內作。

translations.literal: When foreign insult came, the provocation arose from within.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign aggression came with trouble stirred at home.

sentences.zh: 卒使八國連兵，六龍西狩。

translations.literal: In the end eight powers joined arms and the imperial carriage went west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At last the Eight-Nation Alliance marched and the court fled west.

sentences.zh: 庚子以後，怫鬱摧傷，奄致殂落，而國運亦因此而傾矣。

translations.literal: After the year gengzi, depressed and wounded in spirit, he suddenly met his end, and the dynasty's fortune also tilted because of it.
translations.idiomatic: After 1900, brooding and broken, he died suddenly — and the dynasty's fate turned with him.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，豈非天哉！

translations.literal: Alas — was it not Heaven's doing!
translations.idiomatic: Alas — was it not Heaven's will!
